extracted.intended_audience: general readers and the photojournalism community (documentary photographers, visual journalists, students)
extracted.subtask_description: Summary and procedural/mission details for the Pictures of the Year International program and its annual competition, including scope, judging, awards, education programs, exhibitions, and the archive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition scope / eligible formats
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pictures of the Year International Competition is for documentary photography, photojournalism, visual editing, and online multimedia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement defines the program's topical and format scope for entries (i.e., documentary/photojournalistic work, visual editing, and multimedia submissions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Category topics include news, sports and portraits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The contest is organized into topical categories (e.g., news, sports, portraits) under which submitted works are judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission scale and international reach
rubrics_metrics.description: Each year more than 52,000 works are submitted to the contest by photojournalists from 71 nation[s].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the large annual submission volume and international participation, which contextualizes competitiveness and diversity of entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of winners selected
rubrics_metrics.description: During three weeks of judging, a panel of 17 visual journalists selects 240 winners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the selection target (240 winners) from the pool of submissions and provides a quantitative metric of recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging panel composition
rubrics_metrics.description: A panel of 17 visual journalists selects winners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines who evaluates entries—peer/industry professionals (visual journalists)—which informs expected standards and expertise applied in judging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging process transparency and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: The three-week review is set in a public forum, with live webcasting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the public and transparent nature of judging (live webcasting) and the multi-week deliberation period, implying openness to public scrutiny and extended deliberation per entry/category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historic/mission criteria (original purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: The contest's stated purpose was 'to pay tribute to those press photographers and newspapers ... to provide an opportunity for photographers of the nation to meet in open competition; and to compile and preserve ... a collection of the best in current, home-front press pictures.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articulates founding values that guide what the contest seeks to recognize: exemplary press photography, open competition, and archival preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational and career-development programming
rubrics_metrics.description: POYi provides educational and career development symposiums for photojournalists, which include lectures, workshops, one-on-one mentoring and portfolio reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates programmatic offerings tied to the competition aimed at professional development for both professionals and college students; lists seminar cities (e.g., Washington, D.C., Los Angeles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Visions of Excellence exhibitions criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: POYi develops exhibitions entitled Visions of Excellence and themed exhibitions culled from the POYi Archive on topics such as the presidency of the United States, the Olympic Games, and African-American history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that award-winning and archival work is curated into thematic exhibitions shown in galleries, museums, libraries, and schools (examples of venues provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emerging Vision Incentive eligibility/target
rubrics_metrics.description: The Emerging Vision Incentive program provided $10,000 in funding for aspiring or early-career photojournalists to produce in-depth documentary projects that target a specific social issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the funding program's purpose and eligibility focus (aspiring/early-career photographers) and the expectation that funded projects be in-depth documentary investigations of a specific social issue. (Note: page marks citation needed.)

rubrics_metrics.name: POYi Archive: preservation and accessibility standard
rubrics_metrics.description: POYi created a Web platform to host the digital archive of all the winning photographs; the POYi Archive contains more than 40,000 photographs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archive launched in September 2008 in collaboration with the University of Missouri, uses the Omeka CMS, and serves to compile and make accessible past winners—establishing preservation and discoverability as program standards.
